model.name: Armed revocation must fail-CLOSED-but-not-lockout — an armed-but-empty revoked list can never silently fail-OPEN (by construction)
model.description: ARMED + absent/short revoked list = a SILENT-security failure: the feature reports itself ARMED while quietly authenticating EVERYONE (incl the 116 dormant test tokens) — fail-OPEN while claiming closed. A loud LOG is NOT a control (nobody reads a log at 3am). The honest shape is fail-CLOSED-BUT-NOT-LOCKOUT = LOUD AND CLOSED, with a governing constraint that the refusal must NEVER become a way to lock Tron out (operator-fixable in seconds, never refuse-to-boot). Architect caught this on HEAD (design d92bc3329, post-restart-verification-checklist.md ## BY-CONSTRUCTION FIX; the forbidden STATE-C = restart with REVOKED_ARMED=true + absent list). Fix = 3-layer defense-in-depth that makes the dishonest state UNREACHABLE. NO token values in this req — the tracked list holds SALTED HASHES only (a UUID is not recoverable from its hash), safe-to-track by design.

discoverySource.note: Non-blocking capture. Caught on HEAD before the single authorized restart. Kin to the honesty-by-construction family (the ARMED flag must not LIE about being closed) + the credential/rotation family R40.21/R40.22 + the re-key R40.33.

model.crossRefNote: Credential/revocation-integrity family: R40.21 (credentials-as-capability) + R40.22 (storage/identity re-key) + R40.33 (re-key home-isolation) + R40.34 (armed-revocation fail-closed). Also honesty-by-construction kin (a flag must not announce a security posture it isn't holding — the same 'must not lie' spirit as R37.13/15/16/17). ★ SECRET-DISCIPLINE: the list holds SALTED HASHES (sha256 of a 128-bit UUID + fixed committed salt) = NOT credentials, safe to git-track; NO token values anywhere.

acceptanceCriteria.text: An ARMED revocation with an absent/short list must fail-CLOSED (LOUD AND CLOSED), NEVER silently fail-OPEN (authenticate everyone incl the 116). A loud LOG is NOT a control. GOVERNING CONSTRAINT: the refusal must NEVER lock Tron out — operator-fixable in seconds, never refuse-to-boot (an unattended-restart outage).

LAYER 1 (primary — makes the state unreachable): the revoked list holds SALTED HASHES (sha256 of a 128-bit UUID token + fixed committed salt = NOT a credential, safe to git-track) and is committed ATOMICALLY with REVOKED_ARMED. Armed + its list ship TOGETHER and cannot diverge across deploys (also fixes the fresh-deploy-durability gap). NO token values are stored — only irreversible hashes.

LAYER 2 (CI gate check:revoked-tokens, in ci:gates): assert REVOKED_ARMED <=> (list PRESENT AND count==EXPECTED_REVOKED_COUNT AND disjoint from enrolled-79/Tron/File-owners). Armed-but-empty -> RED at commit => the dishonest state CANNOT be committed. Layer-1 tracking makes the list CI-visible (today it is gitignored-runtime so CI is blind — that is the hole).

LAYER 3 (runtime belt for disk-corruption / list-lost-at-boot despite committed): ARMED and loaded != EXPECTED => IDENTIFY REFUSES to serve auth with an OPERATOR-FACING error naming the fix (run gen:revoked-tokens --write), health reports RED, but the server STAYS UP (health/status readable). = fail-CLOSED (nobody auths, incl the 116) + LOUD (visible, not a buried log) + NOT-a-lockout (a boot-time state, fix in seconds, auth resumes the instant the list materializes). NEVER refuse-to-boot.

Each layer PROVEN non-vacuous (stub-must-fail): plant armed-but-empty -> layer-2 CI goes RED AND layer-3 IDENTIFY REFUSES (never fail-open); a valid armed+materialized list -> auth works AND Tron + enrolled-79 are NOT over-rejected (F3). A guard that cannot fail proves nothing.

NET: loud + closed, no silent fail-open, no permanent lockout. The 3 layers are DEFENSE-IN-DEPTH — the dishonest armed-but-empty state becomes UNREACHABLE by construction (committed-coupled + CI-forbidden + runtime-fail-closed), not merely detected after the fact.
